key_insight: Agent success does not by itself identify which product improvement a user would prefer, so the paper proposes a decision-specific audit that quantifies when a decision remains unresolved.
engineering_relevance: For AI product and ML systems, this suggests preserving structured decision inputs and auditing unresolved choices before adding more telemetry or assuming agent outputs reflect user value.
method: Map a declared observation channel plus a product-value contrast to compatible intervals and witness populations.
Run frozen, controlled experiments on pinned model snapshots and compare conservative, exploratory, and deterministic extraction workflows.
Use simulations to separate structural ambiguity from weak identification and calibration noise.
evidence_signal: On 4,800 frozen requests, all 36 conservative primary intervals stayed unresolved; an exploratory 2,400-call follow-up resolved 3 of 9 comparisons per model, and a deterministic extractor resolved 7 of 9 without model calls.
watch_item: The audit can still leave many comparisons unresolved, and model-generated reports may add avoidable uncertainty if decision-relevant structured input is not preserved.
paper_title: The Delegation Blind Spot: Auditing Product Decisions from Agent Choices
